text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging net-oncall (alex) — multiple websocket TIMEOUTs reported for AcmeCorp VPC app-gateway (us-west-2). Auto-detected surge in retries + 502/504 streams. Severity: P1. Links: https://incidents.redwood/acme/3332104567

alex: on it. can someone paste current error rate + which dedicated pool they're on?

sam: quick numbers from logs: 4xx/5xx spike started at 2026-03-15T14:22Z. WS connections failing to upgrade, ~18% stream reconnect rate, retries causing client bursts. tail from gateway: ```[2026-03-15T14:23:01Z] conn=abcd1234 upgrade failed: EOF
[2026-03-15T14:23:02Z] stream=acme-req-988 retry_count=3 backend=appgw-01 502
[2026-03-15T14:23:05Z] conn=abcd1234 close reason=timeout duration=32s```

anya: they're on dedicated-pool-acme-01 (4xA100). No recent deploys on our side since 14:00Z. Metrics show ebpf socket timeouts on host 10.3.2.45.

li: customer ops (customerops-bob) says Acme saw errors in their app logs too, reporting a flurry of websocket retries into their backend after a routing blip. They're escalating with their infra lead. @tilly can you join their bridge?

tilly: joining now. pinged Acme SRE. They confirm a config change to AppGW connection-timeout at ~14:20Z but insist it was minor. Asking if we can throttle retries on our gateway side while they patch.

alex: mitigation plan options: 1) temporarily increase gateway WS idle read timeout / bump keepalive to reduce false closes, 2) flip traffic for Acme to their secondary pool (dedicated-pool-acme-02) and scale it up, 3) enable streaming->long-polling fallback for Acme tenant, 4) apply per-tenant retry caps (throttle) at edge. Which is fastest?

anya: fastest = enable streaming->longpoll fallback per tenant (no client changes) + apply per-tenant retry cap 3. Command to enable fallback: ```rwctl tenant update acme --streaming-fallback longpoll``` to cap retries: ```rwctl tenant update acme --retry-cap 3``` This will reduce backend pressure immediately.

infra-bot: Rate limiter policy for acme currently default. To update and apply immediately run: ```infra apply-policy --tenant acme --policy retry-cap=3 --propagate now```

sam: I'll run the fallback + retry cap now. prepping to divert if that doesn't land in 90s.

sam: (executed) ```rwctl tenant update acme --streaming-fallback longpoll && rwctl tenant update acme --retry-cap 3``` 

incident-bot: action logged by sam at 2026-03-15T14:26:40Z — fallback + retry-cap applied. Notifying customer.

customerops-bob: saw immediate drop in backend error spikes on our side ~14:27Z. clients started reconnecting with fewer retries. partial recovery observed.

tilly: Acme SRE on bridge says longpoll fallback is holding and backend 502s decreased. They're going to roll back their recent AppGW timeout tweak and will report when done.

alex: good. still need to reduce risk of recurrence. next steps: 1) keep fallback + retry cap for 30m, 2) scale dedicated-pool-acme-02 and consider routing 20% traffic there while Acme reverts change, 3) collect pcap/traces for host 10.3.2.45, 4) postmortem with customer and ops.

anya: capturing traces now. `tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/acme_ws_14-26.pcap host 10.3.2.45` and exporting to s3://redwood-incidents/acme/3332104567/trace.pcap

sam: I'll coordinate brief traffic split: `rwctl route set --tenant acme --split 80:20 --pools dedicated-pool-acme-01,dedicated-pool-acme-02` — applying in 2m.

alex: if split looks good, we'll keep split until Acme confirms their config rollback. assign oncall handoff to nixt (next on-call) at 15:00Z. nixt, FYI you'll get a pager if error rate rebounds >5% 5m sustained.

incident-bot: oncall-handoff scheduled: from alex -> nixt at 2026-03-15T15:00Z. Paging threshold set.

tilly: customer confirmed they reverted AppGW timeout change at 14:40Z. monitoring for 10m then will notify.

sam: split applied. traffic metrics: within 90s of split, pool02 CPU at 30% and connections stable.

customerops-bob: Acme says user-facing impact reduced to <1% request errors. thank you.

alex: leaving note: incident mitigated by fallback + retry cap + traffic split. suspected contributing cause: customer-side timeout change provoking client retries which amplified into a retry storm at our gateway host with transient socket timeouts. root cause TBD after traces. assigning postmortem owners: sam (infra), anya (runtime), tilly (customer liaison).

tilly: will schedule 1h follow-up with Acme tomorrow EOD.

sam: grabbing pcap and logs, will attach to incident ticket: https://incidents.redwood/acme/3332104567/ticket

alex: handing off. nixt, please keep fallback until we confirm full rollback + clean metrics for 60m. If errors reappear, escalate to oncall-sre.

incident-bot: thread closed for real-time updates. Post any follow-ups in #postmortems-acme or reopen incident thread if regression seen. :white_check_mark:
